record.name: Next-token supervision from raw sequences
record.role: Construct shifted next-token targets and interpret token likelihood separately from answer accuracy.
record.description: Autoregressive pretraining asks a model to predict each next token from earlier inputs. The target is the shifted sequence, not the token already visible at the same position. Summing negative log probabilities gives a sequence score; averaging included targets gives the training objective. Exponentiating this mean yields perplexity under the same tokenization and mask. Answer accuracy is a different measurement: it observes selected decisions rather than every token probability. A model can become better at punctuation or repeated format markers while its answer decisions remain unchanged.
mechanism: Pair input position t with token t+1 and mark valid targets.
Compute stable log-softmax and gather each target’s log probability.
Sum losses and divide by included targets across the batch.
Fit a simple baseline on training data only and compare the same reserved targets.
record.learningObjective: Construct shifted next-token targets and interpret token likelihood separately from answer accuracy.
record.engineeringExample: For three target probabilities [1/2,1/4,1/2], total NLL is ln2+ln4+ln2=ln16=2.772589 nats. Mean NLL is 0.924196 nats and perplexity is 16^(1/3)=2.519842. A uniform nine-token predictor has mean NLL ln9=2.197225 and perplexity 9. Feeding the answer token at the very position being scored would invalidate this comparison through target leakage.
record.evidenceNotes: Mode: executable core. Natural logarithms, positive target probabilities and nonzero denominator. Perplexities with different tokenization/masks are not directly comparable. Numerical examples are authored calculations, except explicitly identified automated core fixtures. Primary sources support the scoped mechanism; no human specialist review or learner outcome is implied.
